financials_interim.notes: Janashakthi Finance PLC (BFN, formerly Orient Finance PLC) is a licensed finance company (NBFI) -- single entity, no Group/Company split. Filing is presented in Rs.'000; all figures below are converted to absolute Rupees (x1,000) for this row, per project convention. shares_in_issue = 211,101,155 ordinary shares, disclosed exactly (Stated Capital note, 'No. of Ordinary Shares'). Cross-checked: EPS 90,413,000/211,101,155 = 0.4283, rounds to disclosed 0.43; NAVPS 4,097,636,000/211,101,155 = 19.41, ties disclosed 19.41 exactly. No column-swap issues found. revenue = 'Total operating income' (933,258,000), the filing's own subtotal = Net interest income (880,373,000) + Fee and commission income (50,045,000) + Other operating income (2,840,000). operating_profit = 'Operating profit/(loss) before Value Added Tax' (212,696,000), the company's own pre-VATFS subtotal. finance_costs/finance_income left BLANK -- Interest income (1,832,133,000) and Interest expenses (951,760,000) are disclosed as separate gross lines but netted to an explicit 'Net interest income' subtotal before Total operating income (same structure as AFSL/ALLI/AMF/CDB/AAF this session), so populating them separately would double count against revenue. tax_expense = 'Income tax expense' (47,798,000) only; 'Tax on financial services' (74,485,000) is a separate VAT-on-Financial-Services-type levy sitting between operating_profit and profit_before_tax, consistent with this session's other NBFI entries. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per NBFI convention -- liquidity-ordered balance sheet, no current/non-current split; 'Loans and receivables at amortised cost' (34,450,592,000) is the core lending book across five segments (Finance leases & HP, Loans, Factoring, Gold Loan, Others), not a trade receivable. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks - bank overdrafts' (1,417,451,000), explicitly labelled as overdrafts, unambiguously short-term (also confirmed by the cash flow statement's Note A, which nets bank overdrafts of 1,417,451,000 against cash on hand/at bank to reach a NEGATIVE cash-and-equivalents figure of (976,733,000) -- that cash-flow-statement definition is broader than the Balance Sheet 'Cash and cash equivalents' line used for cash_and_equivalents below, and is not used here to avoid reporting negative cash). long_term_borrowings = 'Interest bearing borrowings' (14,805,485,000), a separate general borrowings line distinct from the overdraft and from customer deposits; no further maturity split is disclosed on this condensed balance sheet, so this is an approximation (consistent with how this session treated LOFC's undifferentiated borrowings line), cross-checked against the cash flow statement's 'Interest bearing borrowings obtained' (6,800,120,000) and 'Repayment of interest bearing borrowings' (5,621,009,000) during the quarter, which are sizeable roll-overs consistent with structured term funding rather than short-dated facilities. 'Deposits from customers' (18,271,774,000) is deliberately EXCLUDED from borrowings -- deposit funding, not debt, per project convention. 'Lease liability - right of use assets' (445,319,000) is also excluded, consistent with this session's treatment of small lease liabilities for other NBFIs. cash_and_equivalents = Balance Sheet 'Cash and cash equivalents' (440,719,000); see above re: the broader, overdraft-inclusive cash-flow-statement definition which nets to a negative figure and is not used here. capex = 'Acquisition of property, plant and equipment and intangible assets' (13,032,000) -- disclosed as a single combined cash-flow line, cannot be disaggregated into PP&E vs intangibles from this filing (a genuine gap, noted below). Impairment/NPL commentary: 'Impairment charges for loans and receivables at amortised cost' rose from Rs.78,388,000 (Q1 FY25/26) to Rs.95,508,000 (Q1 FY26/27), +21.9%, but the segment note (p.5) shows this was NOT broad-based: Gold Loan segment impairment actually fell sharply, from Rs.27,105,000 to just Rs.989,000 (-96%), while the 'Others' segment swung from a Rs.0 impairment charge to Rs.20,068,000 and the core Finance Leases & Hire Purchase segment impairment rose 37% (Rs.47,531,000 to Rs.65,240,000) on a book that grew 32% YoY (segment assets Rs.18,083,894,000 to Rs.23,906,072,000). Depreciation and amortisation also rose sharply, +65% (Rs.48,977,000 to Rs.80,743,000), and Personnel expenses +22% (Rs.225,044,000 to Rs.274,297,000) -- together with the impairment increase, these operating-expense increases explain why Profit before tax rose only 27% (Rs.108,786,000 to Rs.138,211,000) despite Total operating income growing a much stronger 24% and Net interest income growing 26%. The filing itself flags (note 3) that the comparative 31 March 2026 balance sheet figures included here are UNAUDITED and subject to the ongoing year-end audit review process -- a genuine disclosed uncertainty, noted as a gap.
